factors.name: Size and parallel branching
factors.summary: Number of empty sequence flows (0.92), Token split (0.84), Size (0.82), Control flow complexity (0.72) and Connector Mismatch (0.71) load highly, so this factor combines net size with the amount of splitting, especially parallel splitting. It is the strongest factor (37% of variance). Size also loads 0.53 on Factor 3, and Control flow complexity cross-loads on Factor 2 (0.60).

factors.name: Connector degree and connectivity
factors.summary: Maximum connector degree (0.87), Coefficient of network connectivity (0.79) and Control flow complexity (0.60, cross-loading with Factor 1) define this factor. It reflects how many arcs attach to nodes, both at the widest connector and on average per node. Token split also loads moderately (0.46) but is assigned to Factor 1.

factors.name: Sparsity and separability
factors.summary: Density loads negatively (-0.79) and Separability positively (0.64), so nets scoring high are sparse relative to their possible arcs and have few articulation points. Size loads 0.53 on this factor, which fits the fact that density shrinks as nets grow. It rests on only two assigned measures, so the interpretation is moderate.

factors.name: Sequentiality
factors.summary: This factor is carried almost entirely by Sequentiality (0.95). Other loadings are small, the highest being Coefficient of network connectivity at 0.17. Its eigenvalue before rotation (0.53) is below 1, and Sequentiality shows a possible Heywood case, so this is a weak, single-measure factor.

interpretation.overall: Bartlett's test is significant and the overall KMO of 0.82 exceeds 0.6, so the data are suitable for factor analysis. Four varimax factors explain 85% of the variance: a dominant size/parallel-branching factor, a connector-degree/connectivity factor, a sparsity/separability factor, and a single-measure sequentiality factor. All measures are assigned. Control flow complexity cross-loads on Factors 1 and 2, and Size has a secondary loading on Factor 3. The fourth factor goes beyond the three that were suggested.
caveats: Four factors were extracted although three were suggested, and the fourth eigenvalue is 0.53, so Factor 4 may be over-extraction.
Sequentiality has a communality at the bound of the fit (possible Heywood case), so Factor 4's loading should be treated with caution.
Connector Heterogeneity and Average connector degree were removed by the MSA filter, and Number of duplicate tasks was constant, so these aspects are not represented.
Factor 3 rests on only two assigned measures and Factor 4 on one, which limits how reliably they can be interpreted.
The results reflect shared variance in these 288 discovered nets under varimax rotation and do not imply causal dimensions.
